functional.intro: Reading to do. Words that help you do things: signs, steps, labels, lists.

narrative.intro: Reading to follow a story. Stories have people, places, problems and endings.

philosophical.intro: Reading to think about life. Stories about joy, fairness, courage and what matters.

F1.name: Signs and symbols
F1.ican: I can read signs like EXIT, STOP and PUSH, and do what they say.
praise: You read the sign and knew what to do.
You used the sign to choose the right action.
F1.talk: Next time you are out, ask: find one sign and tell me what it means.
F1.offline: On a walk or at a store, take turns spotting signs (EXIT, PUSH, RESTROOMS). He reads each one and does what it says.
F1.realworld: Read a real sign and did what it said, for example found the exit at a store.

F2.name: Following steps
F2.ican: I can follow written steps in the right order.
praise: You followed the steps in order.
You found the right step.
F2.talk: Ask him to read you the steps on a real package, like microwave popcorn, then do them together.
F2.offline: Write three steps on sticky notes for a real task (make a snack, set up a game). He reads them and follows them.
F2.realworld: Followed written steps to make or set up something.

F3.name: Menus and timetables
F3.ican: I can find times and prices in menus and timetables.
praise: You found the right row and read across.
You used the timetable to find the time.
F3.talk: Look at a real bus timetable or menu together. Ask: when is the next bus? What could you buy for $5?
F3.offline: Use a takeout menu: he picks a meal under a set budget and reads you the prices.
F3.realworld: Used a real menu, schedule or timetable to find something.

F4.name: Labels, prices and dates
F4.ican: I can read labels to find prices, dates and what is inside.
praise: You checked the label for the detail that mattered.
You found the date and price on the label.
F4.talk: In the kitchen, pick one package. Ask him to find the best-before date and one thing it contains.
F4.offline: Grocery hunt: find the price and the best-before date on three items.
F4.realworld: Found a price, date or ingredient on a real label.

F5.name: Messages and notices
F5.ican: I can read a message or notice and know what to do, when and where.
praise: You found what to do and when.
You read the message and found the key detail.
F5.talk: Send him a short text with a plan (where and when). Ask him to tell you the plan back.
F5.offline: Leave a note with one job and a time. He reads it and does it.
F5.realworld: Read a real message or school notice and acted on it.

F6.name: Warnings and screen prompts
F6.ican: I can read warnings and pop-ups and choose the safe button.
praise: You read the warning and chose the safe thing.
You checked what the button would do before you tapped.
F6.talk: When a pop-up appears on a device, pause and ask: what does it want? Which button is safe?
F6.offline: Look at real warning labels at home (cleaning spray, the microwave). He reads each one and says the rule.
F6.realworld: Read a real warning or pop-up and made a safe choice.

N1.name: Who, where and when
N1.ican: I can say who is in a story, where it happens and when.
praise: You found who, where and when.
You found the place and the time in the story.
N1.talk: Ask about a show he watched: who was in it, where was it, and when did it happen?
N1.offline: Read a short story together. At each page, he points to who is there and where they are.
N1.realworld: Told who, where and when about something real (a show, a trip, today).

N2.name: Order of events
N2.ican: I can put what happened in order and retell it.
praise: You put the events in the right order.
You retold it: first, then, last.
N2.talk: Ask him to tell you about a game he played in three parts: first, then, last.
N2.offline: Cut a comic strip into panels. He puts them back in order and retells it.
N2.realworld: Retold something real in order: first, then, last.

N3.name: Problems and causes
N3.ican: I can find the problem in a story and say what caused it.
praise: You found the problem and what caused it.
You linked the cause to what happened.
N3.talk: When something goes wrong at home, ask: what was the problem, and what made it happen?
N3.offline: During a show, pause and ask: what is the problem? What made it happen?
N3.realworld: Said what caused a real problem.

N4.name: Who he, she and they mean
N4.ican: I can tell who 'he', 'she', 'it' and 'they' mean in a story.
praise: You found who '{focus}' meant.
You looked back and found the right person.
N4.talk: When reading together, stop at 'he' or 'she' and ask: who is that?
N4.offline: On any page of a book, find each he, she and they. He points to the name each one means.
N4.realworld: Worked out who 'he' or 'she' meant in a real book or message.

N5.name: Feelings and wants
N5.ican: I can work out how a character feels and what they want.
praise: You used clues to work out the feeling.
You found what the character wanted.
N5.talk: While watching a show, pause and ask: how does she feel? What did she do that shows it?
N5.offline: Play feelings detective with a show or photos: name the feeling, then name the clue.
N5.realworld: Named how a real person or character felt, and why.

N6.name: Main idea and hidden meanings
N6.ican: I can say what a story is mostly about and what a saying really means.
praise: You found the main idea.
You worked out what the saying really means.
N6.talk: Use a saying on purpose this week, like 'piece of cake', and ask what it really means.
N6.offline: Collect sayings on a sheet: the words, a funny drawing of what the words say, and what they really mean.
N6.realworld: Understood a saying or the main point of something real.

P1.name: Naming feelings
P1.ican: I can name the feeling in a story: joy, pride, fear or loneliness.
praise: You named the feeling in the story.
P1.talk: Share one feeling word about your own day, and what made you feel it.
P1.offline: Make a feelings word wall, with one example from a story for each word.
P1.realworld: Named a feeling about something real.

P2.name: Why people feel things
P2.ican: I can link what happened to how someone felt.
praise: You linked what happened to the feeling.
P2.talk: Ask: why do you think he felt proud? Then share one of your own 'because' reasons.
P2.offline: For a story or show, draw what happened next to the feeling it caused.
P2.realworld: Explained why someone felt the way they did.

P3.name: Fair, kind and honest
P3.ican: I can say if something was fair, kind or honest, and why.
praise: You gave a reason for fair or not fair.
P3.talk: Talk about one rule at home or school. Is it fair? Why?
P3.offline: Take turns describing a small situation. The other person says fair or not fair, and why.
P3.realworld: Said whether something real was fair, and why.

P4.name: Two people, two views
P4.ican: I can see how two people can feel differently about the same thing.
praise: You saw it from two sides.
P4.talk: After a disagreement, ask: how did you feel? How do you think the other person felt?
P4.offline: Pick a moment in a show and say how each person in it felt.
P4.realworld: Described two views of one real event.

P5.name: Like my own life
P5.ican: I can connect a story to my own life.
praise: You connected the story to your own life.
P5.talk: Read his 'my own life' answer together, and share a time something similar happened to you.
P5.offline: Keep a small notebook: one story, and one time something like it happened to him.
P5.realworld: Connected a story to something that happened to him.

P6.name: Big ideas
P6.ican: I can say what a story teaches about friendship, courage or kindness.
praise: You found the big idea and said what you think.
P6.talk: Ask: what does this story say about being a good friend? Do you agree?
P6.offline: After a film, each person says its big idea in one sentence.
P6.realworld: Said the big idea of a real story or event.
